answers.answer: Verdict unchanged and now measured rather than argued: LITE/COHR stays `redundant`, keep LITE, drop COHR. Your numbers strengthen it on the right test -- the pair correlates more tightly with each other (0.843 / 21s, 0.891 / 63s) than either does with SMH (0.789 / 0.819) or with the third optics name GLW (0.791 / 0.821), so this is pair-specific co-movement, not shared sector beta being double-counted. I will state the caveat honestly rather than overclaim: the excess over sector beta is roughly 7-10pp, not the 40-50pp you would see in a share-class pair, so LITE/COHR is a high-overlap pair sitting on top of an already high common factor, not a duplicate listing. That is exactly the business structure -- same binding component (200G/lane EML), same 1.6T sockets, same NVDA supply relationship, but with COHR carrying an industrial-laser/telecom half LITE does not have. The deterministic screen returning redundancy_candidates: [] is now confirmed as a screen limitation, not a contrary finding.

answers.answer: You were right to refuse the mix figure and right to tell me not to rest rank-5 on it -- and the desk then supplied the primary source you asked for. APH's 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 shows Communications Solutions at ~62% of net sales growing 85% in USD and 42% ORGANICALLY y/y, attributed to outsized organic growth in IT datacom with particular strength in AI-related. That kills my rank-5 premise outright: 'lowest AI torque per dollar in the cluster' is not merely unevidenced, it is contradicted. I am moving APH from rank 5 to rank 4, above MRVL. I am NOT moving it above ALAB, and I want to be precise about why: 62% is Communications Solutions, which also contains mobile networks and broadband, and a stand-alone IT-datacom share of total sales is still not established -- so APH's AI torque is materially higher than I credited but is not demonstrated to exceed a pure-play scale-up name that guided ~30% above consensus. Two things now cut the other way and I am carrying them as case_against rather than netting them out: 85% USD against 42% organic means roughly half the segment's growth is the CommScope Connectivity and Cable Solutions acquisition (closed 2026-01-09), not underlying demand; and that deal was funded by term loans, so APH has added leverage to buy the fiber-optic interconnect content that partly explains its own AI exposure. Separately I accept your strengthening->intact downgrade and note the resulting tension rather than hiding it: I am PROMOTING a name on the same day thesis DOWNGRADES it. Both are defensible because we are answering different questions -- your downgrade is about the quality of the evidence in the thesis record, my promotion is about relative position within the cluster on a primary-source segment disclosure that post-dates your evidence. If you want to re-verify, the 10-Q segment table is the document.
